meaning.question: What does it mean to “glorify” God?

meaning.explain: We cannot add to God’s greatness, but we can honor it and show it in what we say and do.

quiz.explain: “The LORD is my shepherd”. Jesus later called Himself the Good Shepherd (John 10:11).

cards.title: The prayer Jesus taught
cards.body: When His disciples asked Him how to pray, Jesus gave them these words. Christians have prayed them every day for two thousand years, and they shape every other prayer.

cards.title: The Lord’s Prayer
cards.body: Five verses from Matthew 6. Each one you learn lights a fifth of the window.

cards.title: How Katekize helps you remember
cards.body: Short lessons. You’ll see each verse, build it, then say or type it from memory. Verses come back just as you’re about to forget them, which is when recalling them helps most.

quiz.question: Who taught the Lord’s Prayer?
quiz.explain: Jesus taught it in the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 6:9–13).

quiz.question: How does the prayer begin?
quiz.explain: Jesus teaches us to come to God as children to their Father.

cards.title: Hear, Israel!
cards.body: “Shema” is Hebrew for “Hear!”, the first word of Deuteronomy 6:4. For three thousand years God’s people have said these words morning and evening, and Jesus called them the greatest commandment.

cards.title: The Blessing
cards.body: The course ends with the blessing God gave the priests to speak over His people: “The LORD bless you, and keep you”.

cards.title: How Katekize helps you remember
cards.body: Short lessons. You’ll see each verse, build it, then say or type it from memory. Verses come back just as you’re about to forget them, which is when recalling them helps most.

quiz.question: What does the Hebrew word “Shema” mean?
quiz.explain: The Shema is named for its first word: “Hear, Israel!”

quiz.question: Which did Jesus call the greatest commandment?
quiz.answer: To love the LORD your God with all your heart
distractors: To give a tenth of everything
To honor your father and mother
quiz.explain: Jesus quoted Deuteronomy 6:5 (Matthew 22:37–38).

cards.title: God’s law
cards.body: God spoke the Ten Commandments from Mount Sinai, and wrote them on two tablets of stone. The first four are about loving God; the last six, about loving our neighbor.

cards.title: Ten verses from Exodus 20
cards.body: One whole verse for each commandment: the verse where it begins. Your cue is its number and reference, such as “The first commandment (Exodus 20:3)”.

cards.title: How Katekize helps you remember
cards.body: Short lessons. You’ll see each verse, build it, then say or type it from memory. Verses come back just as you’re about to forget them, which is when recalling them helps most.

quiz.question: Where did God give the Ten Commandments?
quiz.explain: Moses received them on Mount Sinai (Exodus 19–20).

quiz.question: What were the commandments first written on?
quiz.explain: God wrote them on two tablets of stone (Exodus 31:18).

cards.title: For anxious days
cards.body: Six promises to carry with you: for when you’re afraid, when you’re worried, and when you can’t sleep. They work best learned before you need them.

cards.title: Fear, Worry and Peace
cards.body: The shortest verses come first. Each one you learn lights a sixth of the window.

cards.body: Short lessons. You’ll see each verse, build it, then say or type it from memory. Verses come back just as you’re about to forget them, which is when recalling them helps most.

quiz.question: According to 1 Peter 5:7, why can we give our worries to God?
distractors: Because God is too busy to notice them
quiz.explain: Peter writes: “having cast all your anxiety on Him, because He cares about you.”

quiz.question: When is the best time to learn verses about fear?
quiz.explain: A verse you already know comes back to you when fear does.

cards.title: The good news
cards.body: “Gospel” means good news: that Christ died for our sins and rose again, and that God saves us by grace through faith.

cards.title: The Gospel
cards.body: Six verses that tell it in order: our sin, God’s love, Christ in our place, grace, faith, and new life as God’s children.

quiz.question: What does the word “gospel” mean?
quiz.explain: It comes from an Old English word for “good news”.

quiz.question: How are we saved, according to Ephesians 2:8?
distractors: By being born in a Christian family
quiz.explain: Paul writes: “For by grace you have been saved through faith”.

cards.title: Knowing God
cards.body: Everything else rests on who God is. These six verses say it in the Bible’s own words: He is eternal, unchanging, holy, love, gracious and faithful.

cards.title: Who God Is
cards.body: It pairs well with the Shorter Catechism’s fourth question, “What is God?”. Each verse you learn lights a sixth of the window.

quiz.question: Which of these is true of God?
quiz.answer: He has no beginning and no end
distractors: He began when the world began
He changes His mind about His promises
He is holy only some of the time
quiz.explain: “Even from everlasting to everlasting, You are God” (Psalm 90:2).

quiz.question: Who says “Holy, Holy, Holy” in Isaiah 6?
quiz.explain: Isaiah saw the seraphim calling to one another before the LORD.

cards.title: Easter in six verses
cards.body: From Isaiah’s Servant, pierced for us, to the angel at the empty tomb and the living hope we have because Jesus rose. Begin in Lent and you can say them all by Easter.

cards.title: He is risen
cards.body: Easter is the oldest Christian feast. Christians have greeted each other on Easter morning for centuries: “He is risen!” “He is risen indeed!”

quiz.question: On which day was Jesus raised?
quiz.explain: “He was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures” (1 Corinthians 15:4).

quiz.question: Who told the women that Jesus had risen?
quiz.explain: The angel at the tomb said, “He is not here, for He has risen, just as He said.”
